transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start time: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sasha Nguyen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Clearview CTO), Tom Reynolds (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Diego Martinez (Product)

Summary (auto):
- Demo of Redwood structured output / JSON mode and function/tool-calling patterns.
- Discussed schemas, guardrails, validation, and security implications (KMS, SSO, SOC2).
- Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot benchmark.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this deal. Sasha and Liam are our SEs, they will run the deep parts of the demo. Can everyone briefly intro?
00:20 Aisha: Hi i'm Aisha, CTO at Clearview. We're evaluating inference platforms for our analytics product, main constraints are low tail latency for interactive queries and strict PII retention rules.
00:35 Tom: Tom here. We'll own the benchmarks and integration. We do mostly batch embedding plus a user-facing chat that needs structured JSON outputs for our downstream parsers.
00:50 Sasha: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll show. Today we'll walk through Redwood API JSON mode and the Console, then demo function-calling / tool patterns and discuss guardrails, schemas, and security. We will also touch on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
01:10 Priya: For security, we care about KMS + HSM, audit logs, and SSO SAML. Also data residency — some customer data never leaves the VPC.
01:25 Liam: Noted. We'll show private deployment options and note how audit logs are surfaced in the Console.
01:40 Jordan: Quick agenda: 1) Structured output basics and schema enforcement, 2) Function/tool calling demo for a ticketing workflow, 3) Console inspect and Optimize recommendations.

05:05 Sasha: Ok demo start. Here is the JSON mode request: we attach a schema that expects an object with fields {ticket_id (string), priority (enum), summary (string), actions (array of objects)}. Redwood's runtime will validate output against the schema and can return structured parse failures.
05:30 Sasha: (typing) i'm sending a sample prompt that instructs the model to extract entities from the user's text and map to the schema. Note: some transcription may say "schemas" as "ski mas", sorry.
06:02 System: [automated note] We're showing Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/demo/struct-out (link shared)
06:20 Diego: Quick Q — how strict is the enforcement? If the model outputs a missing field, what happens?
06:32 Sasha: There are modes: "soft" validation (we return the raw text + a parse object with errors) and "strict" validation where the response is rejected and can trigger a fallback model or a structured error to your app. For strict mode we also return the partial KV cache context so you can re-prompt or auto-fix.
07:10 Tom: Do you do auto-correction? Like if priority is "highh" vs "high"?
07:20 Sasha: Yes we have normalization rules and fuzzy enum matching, but in strict mode normalization can be disabled if you want exact matches. There's also a confidence score per field exposed in the response.

09:00 Sasha: Now the function-calling demo. We'll show two patterns: 1) explicit function call — Redwood will call the tool you registered (e.g., create_ticket) with validated JSON payload; 2) agent pattern — model returns a plan and Redwood orchestrates sequential tool calls.
09:25 Jordan: We'll simulate a ticket created in Jira via a tool shim. For demo purposes it's a mock endpoint.
10:05 Sasha: (demo) Model produced call: create_ticket({"summary":"User reported missing export","priority":"high","actions":[{"type":"investigate","owner":"eng-team"}]}) — then we showed the actual outbound webhook to our mock service.
10:45 Aisha: In production we'd want the outbound webhook to be inside our VPC or go through private peering. Can Redwood support that?
10:55 Liam: Yes, for Redwood Private / on-prem we can host the tool connector inside their VPC and use customer-managed networking. For Hosted/Redwood API you can also bring a private connector or use TLS + static IPs and our gateway policies.
11:25 Priya: Does the audit log capture payloads? We need to redact PII.
11:35 Sasha: Audit logs capture metadata by default — API call, user id, model used, time, but payload capture is configurable. You can enable payload retention for debugging, or keep payloads encrypted with your KMS, or set redaction rules that mask PII before storage.
12:05 Diego: How about encryption at rest — HSM support?
12:10 Liam: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM providers; Redwood Private allows you to point to your own KMS and manage keys. For Hosted we can support envelope encryption and customer KMS integration depending on the contract.

15:00 Sasha: Back to structured output — here's an example where we intentionally trigger a schema mismatch. The model returns an extra top-level field "ticket_ref'" (typo) and missing 'priority'. Console shows a parse error and we can configure an auto-correct rule to remap ticket_ref -> ticket_id if confidence high.
15:30 Tom: That's useful. For our pipeline, we want guaranteed valid JSON so our workers don't crash.
15:42 Sasha: For that use case we recommend strict validation + canary rollout with a fallback policy: if schema fails above X% we route to a more deterministic model or to a synchronous human review queue.
16:05 Jordan: Let's show the Console view — it has a per-route schema tab, examples, and an eval harness for regression testing. Sasha, can you open the Evaluate tab?
16:25 Sasha: (typing) Here: evaluate prompt sets. You can upload your own test prompts and Redwood will run them across model variants, report schema pass rate, token cost, and latency. The Optimize tab will recommend quantization and batching settings to hit cost/latency targets.
17:00 Aisha: How granular are the Optimize suggestions? Can it tell us batch sizes for our 99th percentile latency target?
17:10 Liam: Yes, Optimize shows expected latency for different batch sizes and suggests a profile for Dedicated pools. It also recommends model variants (e.g., 7B-qat vs 13B-ptq) based on quality thresholds.

19:20 Sasha: Quick demo: function calling with fallbacks. We configure a fallback policy: if create_ticket returns a 5xx or validation error, Redwood will try alternative model variant or queue the request to a background job with notification.
19:50 Diego: Does Redwood provide SDKs with typed bindings for these function calls?
20:02 Sasha: Yes — SDKs for Python/Node include typed function signatures generated from your schema; they also include client-side validators so you can validate before sending. Some transcriptions may show "node" as "noed" — apologies.

22:15 Tom: For performance, what's the tokenization overhead with structured output? We do many small calls.
22:25 Liam: There's modest overhead for additional metadata, but batching and prefix caching reduce per-token cost. For small, latency-sensitive requests we recommend dedicated capacity with conversational caching.
22:50 Tom: Any numbers?
22:55 Liam: On Dedicated we see p95 latency ~90ms for 8K tokens with optimized kernels on A100-class hardware in our benchmarks for smaller models; for small single-turn schema responses it's often sub-100ms p95 on optimized paths. Your actual numbers will depend on model and input distribution.

25:30 Sasha: Security corner cases — SSO and RBAC. Console supports granular role-based permissions per route, and you can limit who can view payloads or audit logs. Also SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning.
25:55 Priya: We need SCIM for user sync and fine-grained role mapping.
26:10 Jordan: We'll include SCIM and a sample SAML metadata file in the security pack.

28:00 Sasha: Now a quick walkthrough of schema authoring in the Console. You can define JSON schema or Redwood's simplified field definitions (enums, regex, nested arrays). Then you can add a guarded example set.
28:30 Sasha: This is where guardrails live: you can block outputs with PII, set allowed-domain whitelists for external tool calls, and configure entity-level redaction.
29:05 Aisha: Example: we need to prevent exporting customer emails to third-party tools.
29:20 Sasha: You can mark fields as "sensitive"; outbound tool connectors will by default drop or redact those fields unless explicitly allowed in the connector policy.

31:10 Diego: For auditing the function calls, do you log function args?
31:20 Liam: Logs include function call metadata and optionally hashed/anonymized args. There's also an integration for sending logs to your SIEM.
31:35 Priya: We want to ensure the audit chain includes model version + kernel profile for reproducibility.
31:50 Sasha: Console attaches model id, quantization profile, and runtime kernel selection to every request in the trace.

33:40 Sasha: Live Q&A: Diego asks about fallback to human-in-the-loop. We have a built-in escalation that creates a task for your agents when strict validation fails repeatedly.
34:05 Tom: We'll try the benchmarking. What's needed from our side?
34:12 Jordan: Sample prompts, token distribution, and a test VPC endpoint if you want realistic network tests. Tom agreed earlier to send those.
34:30 Tom: I'll send a 2-week sample set and also a small harness to replay requests.
34:45 Jordan: Great. I'll follow up with pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated and a pilot agreement for Redwood Private if needed.
35:10 Sasha: Quick note — sometimes transcripts from Fireflies will mangle acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash), so take a look at the Console screenshots we shared for clarity.

39:00 Jordan: Recap: 1) We'll send pilot pricing and Dedicated options. 2) Sasha to share security pack with SOC2, SAML/SCIM, KMS notes. 3) Tom to send sample workloads for benchmarking. 4) Schedule benchmarking session.
39:25 Aisha: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
39:32 Priya: None after reviewing security pack, but we need to validate KMS flow.
39:45 Jordan: We'll include that in our doc.

41:00 Diego: One last question — for the agent pattern, can we enforce per-tool rate limits?
41:10 Liam: Yes, Redwood supports per-connector rate limits and queuing policies. Also you can set cost guards to prevent runaway billings.
41:30 Aisha: That's important.

43:00 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up. End meeting.
